question.text: This man conquered several Sumerian city-states in the 24th and 23rd centuries BCE. It was under him that the Akkadian Empire reached its greatest height.
question.answerHtml: Sargon the Great [or Sargon I, or Sargon of Akkad; prompt on Sargon]
question.clue: He appointed his daughter Enheduanna high priestess, and his empire reached its greatest expanse under his grandson Naram-sin.

swap.leadin: The sun god Shamash [SHAH-mahsh] is depicted on a black basalt monument giving this set of laws to its namesake.
swap.text: Name this Akkadian legal code engraved on a stele [STEE-lee] that is named for a Babylonian king. It has 282 laws, including the well-known ones about an eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.
swap.clue: Jean-Vincent Scheil discovered most of it at Susa in 1901, on a stela which also depicts its namesake on the Shamash throne and is written in cuneiform.

question.text: Two Akkadian-speaking empires followed the original Akkadian empire. They were Babylon and this empire centered at Nineveh.
question.clue: Major rulers of this empire included Tiglath-Pilesar III and Sennacherib.

swap.leadin: Nebuchadnezzar had the Hanging Gardens engineered in this city for his wife Amytis, who felt homesick.
swap.text: Name this ancient city located on the Euphrates River.
swap.clue: His son built great works like the Etemenanki ziggurat and a blue tiled gate which served as the northern entrance to this city.

question.leadin: Their original version may have been built by the Assyrian king Sennacherib in his capital of Nineveh.
question.text: Name this Wonder of the Ancient World believed to be built by a king for his Median wife, Queen Amytis, because she missed the hills and valleys of her homeland.
question.clue: According to Strabo, an early version of Archimedes' Screw was built for use at this location.

swap.text: The Sumerian king list states this figure ruled between king Dumuzid and his own son Ur-Nungal. In an ancient story, this figure loses his friend Enkidu and learns the secret of immortality.
swap.clue: The British ambassador to Tewodros was Hormuzd Rassam, an Assyrian archaeologist who discovered the clay tablets containing this work about a king of Uruk, the oldest known piece of literature.

question.leadin: This civilization's Ubaid period is said to have been developed from the Samarra culture.
question.text: Identify this civilization whose last king was Lugal-Zage-Si and whose Jemdat Nasr period followed its Uruk period. It developed cuneiform.
question.clue: This civilization was the first to farm year-round by employing irrigation canals, and its priesthood worshipped Anu and Inanna.

swap.leadin: This term, which designates much of the Levant, was coined in the early 1900s by archaeologist James Henry Breasted.
swap.text: Give this two-word English name for the "cradle of civilization" that spanned the lower Nile and Mesopotamia.
swap.clue: This region in the Middle East that gets its name from its shape and rich soil, sometimes known as the "cradle of civilization".

question.leadin: The expansion of the culture based in this city can be traced through its distinctive beveled-rim bowl, and it contained temples devoted to Anu and Inanna.
question.text: Identify this city, whose probably legendary rulers included Lugalbanda and his semi-divine son, Gilgamesh.
question.clue: The Ubaid period preceded this city's namesake "Protoliterate" period.

swap.text: Aside from Parthia's Seven Great Houses, the Sassanids took over the capital Ctesiphon, which the Parthians built on this river. This river bounds Mesopotamia with the Euphrates.
swap.clue: This river which flowed through the capital of multiple Persian empires. Along with the Euphrates, this river forms the boundary of Mesopotamia.

question.text: The Gutians ended the reign of this kingdom, which was most famously ruled by Sargon.
question.clue: This native language of the Assyrian and Babylonian empires. It was spoken in a namesake empire founded by Sargon over four thousand years ago.

swap.leadin: The rise of this civilization was preceded by the Ubaid period.
swap.text: Name this civilization, in which the Epic of Gilgamesh was first composed on cuneiform tablets. This civilization built stepped ziggurats at cities like Nippur and Uruk.
swap.answerHtml: Sumer [or sag̃-gíg; accept Sumerian civilization; accept Sumeria; prompt on Mesopotamia or Mesopotamian civilization]
swap.clue: This civilisation was conquered by the Akkadians around 2270 BC, but its language continued in sacral use, written in cuneiform.

question.text: A law-code for this city was written by Urukagina, who was called the "first reformer" for his efforts against corruption and poverty. This city was home to many statues of its king Gudea, as well as the Stele of the Vultures, which details its conflict with neighboring Umma.
question.clue: This city-state was home to the Ibgal temple complex, adjacent to which is the first known brewery.

swap.leadin: In 1852, Hormuzd Rassam discovered a second section of this institution in the Ottoman Vilayet of Mosul.
swap.text: Name this collection whose discovery is attributed to Assyriologist Austen Layard. This collection found at the site of Nineveh included copies of the Enuma Elish and Poor Man of Nippur.
swap.clue: Like a similar institution at Tell el-Amarna, this institution preserved one of the only known versions of "Adapa and the South Wind" as well as several objects "baked" in a post-Carcemish sack.

question.leadin: Mathieu Ossendrijver translated tablets from this culture which compute displacement from a velocity graph by calculating the area underneath the curve in a manner that resembles rudimentary calculus.
question.text: Name this civilization whose study of astronomy is recorded in treatises like the MUL.APIN. The saros cycle of eclipses was first identified by this civilization, whose Plimpton 322 tablet contained a list of Pythagorean triples.
question.answerHtml: Babylonian Empire [accept Old Babylonian Empire or Neo Babylonian Empire; accept Chaldean Dynasty]
question.clue: That successor started this empire's namesake "captivity" after conquering the Kingdom of Judah.

swap.text: The third Assyrian king of this name conquered most of the known world in the 700s BC before his defeat by the Babylonians.
swap.clue: The third king of this name appointed eunuchs as governors (+) and decreased the size of individual provinces in order to weaken subordinates.

question.leadin: The Amarna letters contain a diplomatic correspondence between Amenhotep III and a king of this Hurrian polity named Tushratta.
question.text: Identify this Mesopotamian kingdom with capital at Washukanni. Its greatest king was Saustatar.
question.clue: King Tushratta of this kingdom attempted to solidify an alliance with Egypt through the marriage of his daughter but he was assassinated by one of his sons after the fall of Carchemish.

swap.text: This early Neo-Assyrian ruler led a major subjection of Urartu circa 735 BC during the reign of Rakhianu ("rack"-ee-AH-noo). He had himself named King Pulu after capturing the ruler of Babylon, and he fathered the two rulers who succeeded him, Shalmaneser V (SHAHL-muh-NESS-ur "the fifth") and Sargon II.
swap.clue: This ruler's major campaigns included the subjection of Urartu in 735 B.C.E., and the capture of Damascus during the rebellion of Rakhianu.

question.leadin: He destroyed Susa after conquering the Elamites and sacked Babylon after his brother, Shamash-shum-ukin, rebelled against him.
question.text: Name this Assyrian ruler, who came to the throne when Esarhaddon died in Egypt.
question.clue: One relief from this man's palace shows his queen sitting in front of him while he reclines; that relief is in a garden with a rebel's severed head.

swap.leadin: This activity often took place in an ambassu with many spectators viewing it.
swap.text: Name this activity in which Assyrian rulers symbolically recreated one of Ninurta's deeds. A series of reliefs of this activity shows wine being poured onto the heads of some of its participants.
swap.answerHtml: lion hunting [accept Panthera leo persica in place of “lion”; prompt on hunting; prompt on bird hunting or eagle hunting by asking “with what other animal is the Anzû bird commonly associated?”]
